title: Regional failover drill scenario library and restore verification
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable scenario library and verified restore checklist for scheduled active-passive failover drills. This ticket captures the canonical scenarios (region pairs, service blast-radius, and failure modes), the exact backup/restore verification steps for stateful pieces (metadata stores, object store, KV cache snapshots), expected SLO guardrails to validate during each drill, and circuit-breaker/load-shedding configurations to test graceful degradation. Goal: enable ops teams to run repeatable drills with automated verification and a clear rollback path so that DR confidence and runbook coverage increase across the stack.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario library (documented) covering at least 6 distinct failure modes is published to the DR runbook section in Confluence
Restore verification checklist executes end-to-end for primary DB (Postgres), object store (s3), and KV cache warmup with automated smoke tests
Each scenario includes concrete SLO targets (availability, p95/p99 latency) and pass/fail logic for automated post-drill validation
Circuit breaker and load-shedding toggles can be exercised in a drill and observed in telemetry; at least one policy is validated per scenario
A rollback plan and post-drill action items are added to the scenario and a follow-up retro is scheduled
implementation_notes: High-level approach: 1) Collate existing runbooks and previous drill artifacts into a canonical template. 2) Define scenario metadata: name, scope, blast radius, steps, preconditions, verification queries, SLOs, rollback. 3) Implement small automation helpers: a) restore-verifier script that runs DB checksums, object counts, and synthetic inference probe; b) traffic-generator that can mark requests with priorities to test load-shedding. 4) Wire verification outputs into an ephemeral Slack thread and a drill CI job that emits a drill report artifact.
drill_playbook_steps: Pre-drill: announce window, snapshot production metadata, coordinate with on-call and SRE rotation
Step 0: Confirm recent successful backups for Postgres, S3 model artifacts, and KV snapshot (>= last 24h)
Step 1: Disable write traffic to primary by flipping traffic-router to passive mode (or use maintained traffic-cut flag)
Step 2: Promote regional passive target (secondary) and ensure database failover / replica promotion completes
Step 3: Run restore-verifier: DB checksum, sample rows validation, S3 object manifest compare, KV cache warmup with prefix caching smoke requests
Step 4: Run synthetic workload at small load to validate p95/p99 latency and error budget consumption against SLOs
Step 5: Exercise circuit breaker behavior by artificially injecting increased tail latency on a model-serving shard and observe fallback paths
Step 6: Validate load-shedding by marking low-priority requests in traffic generator, increase QPS until shedding occurs, confirm low-priority rejects while high-priority succeeds
Step 7: Capture traces, logs, and SLO dashboard snapshots; run automated post-checks and publish drill-report artifact
Step 8: Rollback to primary (if scheduled) or keep passive for extended soak if planned; run final integrity checks
rollback_plan: If promotion to secondary has functional regressions (defined by acceptance criteria failures), immediately revert router config to route traffic back to primary. If revert fails, escalate to DB/SRE on-call for manual topology rollback. Steps: 1) abort any remaining synthetic load. 2) run rollback script to re-point LB to original region; 3) run health checks (smoke inference, DB consistency) before re-enabling write traffic; 4) file incident if rollback cannot complete within 30 minutes. Post-rollback: preserve all logs and snapshots for post-mortem and tag as 'drill-rollback'.
test_matrix: Scenario A: AZ outage in primary region -> promote single secondary region. Expected RTO: <= 15m, RPO: <= 5m (replication lag acceptable)
Scenario B: Full region blackhole (control plane reachable only via VPN) -> manual promotion. Expected RTO: <= 30m, validate manual checkpoints
Scenario C: Master DB corruption simulated (logical delete of 1% of test rows) -> restore from snapshot and verify row counts and rewrites
Scenario D: KV cache cold-start after restore -> verify prefix cache warmup completes within 2x normal warmup time and that first-request latency policy triggers graceful queueing
Scenario E: Model artifact mismatch after restore -> verify integrity hash for model tarball and revert to prior artifact if mismatch
Scenario F: Traffic surge during failover -> validate load-shedding rejects <P2 requests and preserves P0/P1 throughput
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards to capture during drill: SLO dashboard (availability, p95/p99 latency per route), error-rate per model, DB replication lag, KV cache hit-rate, LB routing events. Alerts to silence during controlled drills must be configured as part of pre-drill checklist; however, critical alerts (full DB down, data-loss indicators) must remain unmuted. Drill CI job will take snapshots of dashboards and upload to the drill artifact bucket.

post_drill_actions: Every drill produces a checklist of follow-ups: 1) Incident-style postmortem if acceptance criteria failed, 2) Update runbook gaps, 3) Add test coverage for any manual steps automated during the drill, 4) Share lessons with product stakeholders if customer-facing SLOs were impacted.
notes: Keep scenarios small and incremental. Preference for automating verification steps first (restore-verifier) so we can run quick nightly validation for low-risk scenarios. Coordinate with Dedicated infra and Private teams for VPC-sensitive restores. For model-serving fallbacks, ensure model-variant compatibility is tested before promoting traffic.
